Record date: 2128-10-15
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 10/15/28 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD management, evaluation of renal function, and reassessment of mental health status.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for follow-up approximately two weeks after his last visit. He reports that his respiratory symptoms have stabilized, with no significant exacerbations since the last appointment. He continues to use his albuterol inhaler three times daily, but notes that the exertional dyspnea persists during physical activities, particularly when climbing stairs or walking briskly. The cough remains productive with clear sputum, and he denies any hemoptysis.
The bilateral lower extremity edema persists, although Mr. Fairfax reports that he has been more diligent with dietary sodium restrictions and has attempted to increase his fluid intake. He describes the swelling as uncomfortable, rating it 5/10, and he has managed to lose 1 pound since the last visit, which is a positive change in the context of his fluid retention.
Regarding his mental health, Mr. Fairfax reports a slight improvement in mood, attributing this to the recent engagement in cognitive-behavioral therapy sessions. He still experiences insomnia but notes that he has been able to fall asleep more easily, although he wakes several times during the night.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + mild dyspnea, + productive cough, + wheezing, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain, + persistent bilateral lower extremity edema. Neurological - + anxiety, + insomnia, no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, currently using three times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 2 puffs twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 160 mg daily (no change). 7. Sertraline 150 mg daily (no change). 8. Prednisone 40 mg daily for COPD exacerbation (completed course).
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.6F, HR 75, BP 130/80, RR 18, O2 sat 85% on room air.
General: Elderly male in mild respiratory distress, appears fatigued but more engaged. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, mild wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 2+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 9.0, Hgb 10.6, Hct 31.0, Plt 215. 2. BMP: Na 135, K 4.5, Cl 98, CO2 23, BUN 42, Cr 2.4, Glucose 88. 3. BNP: 680 (decreased). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 2.4 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Mr. Fairfax demonstrates stabilization of respiratory symptoms. Continue current inhaler regimen. A follow-up pulmonary function test is scheduled for next month to evaluate lung function post-exacerbation. Referral to pulmonary rehabilitation remains active to enhance exercise tolerance and improve overall quality of life. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. The serum creatinine shows slight improvement. Close monitoring of renal function will continue with follow-up in 1 month for reassessment. 3. Lower extremity edema: The edema has improved slightly with weight loss. Continue furosemide at the current dose and reinforce dietary sodium restrictions. Daily weight monitoring will be encouraged, and nephrology follow-up will be pursued as needed. 4. Mental health: Mr. Fairfax will continue with sertraline at 150 mg daily. Follow-up with psychiatry is ongoing, and he will continue cognitive-behavioral therapy to address anxiety and insomnia.
Patient education reiterated regarding the importance of recognizing exacerbation signs, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
